🇲🇽⚖️ <u>CNDH Inspects 26 Migrant Stations and Finds Fewer Abuses</u>

Mexico's National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) inspected 26 National Migration Institute (INM) facilities for its 2025 Diagnosis, including Siglo XXI in Tapachula, Las Agujas in Iztapalapa, Guadalupe in Nuevo León and the Nuevo Laredo station. It found better infrastructure, maintenance and civil protection, and fewer of the bad practices that once triggered its recommendations. CNDH head Rosario Piedra Ibarra called for more medical, psychological and legal support so detained migrants know their legal situation. INM is drafting a new Migration Law built around the dignity of people on the move, and inspectors check the 36-hour maximum stay.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Foreign Tourists Will Pay 1,158 Pesos to Enter Mexico. Most of It Goes to Defense</u>

Mexico's Chamber of Deputies approved the 2027 Federal Fees Law, raising the Non-Resident Fee (DNR) charged to foreign tourists and short-term visitors by 17.8%, from 983 to 1,158 pesos, about $63. The committee halved the government's original proposal of a 35% increase. Of what the fee collects, 57% goes to the Defense Ministry, 15% to the National Migration Institute for border technology and migration control, and 28% to the Treasury.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Mexico's Supreme Court: Children's Health Comes Before Junk-Food Sales</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court upheld the ban on junk food in every school in the national education system, including prepas and universities. It unanimously threw out a challenge from Eric Kayser México, the Maison Kayser bakery chain, which argued the SEP and Health guidelines of September 30, 2024 violated its freedom of commerce. The Court ruled that the right to health and nutritious food outranks commercial interests. Products with warning labels, sodas and sugary drinks stay out of schools. The ban rests on the 2023 reform to articles 75 and 75 Bis of the General Education Law. Chips and soda can still be sold outside the school gate.

🇲🇽🌎 "Others, no, because they already border on issues that we consider the government of the United States has no reason to be giving its opinion on." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 More than a year ago Washington asked Mexico to resolve 54 trade "barriers," as the US calls them. Sheinbaum said Mexico moved jointly on those that also benefit Mexico, and checks every new demand against whether it suits Mexico and fits its Constitution and laws. Before her last call with Trump, on September 16, Mexico considered everything resolved; Trump raised the trade deficit again. Mexico is shifting purchases toward the US. "President Trump knows that we are the country that buys the most from the United States." Talks with the US Trade Representative and the Commerce Department continue, with no full agreement yet.

text: 🇲🇽🔍 "No opponent is investigated. That has to be very, very clear... Here no one is investigated for political reasons." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Asked how the National Intelligence Center (CNI) contributes to pacifying the country, Sheinbaum recalled that through the 20th century and until 2018, CISEN and before it the Federal Security Directorate of the Interior Ministry were "dedicated, rather, to watching opponents of the regime." The CNI, created under López Obrador, has since been oriented by law toward public security, within the new national system of intelligence and investigation. "Before, they were also dedicated to investigating opponents and their own people." The security cabinet reported some 24,000 CNI alerts this term to prevent homicides, kidnappings and clashes.

🇲🇽🌎 "What is the agreement we have with the United States? It is: give me the early warning, and I guarantee that I will stop it." — Admiral Raymundo Pedro Morales, Secretary of the Navy, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Asked how the Navy works with the US Coast Guard after this week's cocaine seizure off Oaxaca, Morales said a Coast Guard plane spotted the boat off El Salvador and passed on the information; Mexican ships and aircraft intercepted it. Mexico has agreed with Washington that the US will not carry out actions in Mexican maritime zones, including the exclusive economic zone, "because we can do it ourselves." Asked whether the boat could have been blown up by a US missile, as has happened elsewhere: "That is what we are trying to avoid." They could mistake a drug boat for a fishing boat, "which would be very serious."

🇲🇽🌎 "They say we are being left all alone in Latin America. Well, not so much, right? The people protect us, just as we protect the people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 13, 2026 Sheinbaum closed Tuesday's mañanera, with the full security cabinet on stage, by putting up a chart published the day before. "We'll just leave it there."
